items.q: When can I renew my visa?
items.a: You can apply from three months before your period of stay expires. Prepare early to avoid last-minute rush.

items.q: What if my visa expires while renewal is pending?
items.a: If you have filed a renewal, you may remain in Japan until a decision is made (special exception). Carry your passport with the application receipt stamp.

items.q: Do I need to change my status if I change jobs?
items.a: If the new job is within the same activity scope/status, a change is usually unnecessary. If the occupation changes, you need a "Change of Status of Residence".

items.q: What happens if I quit my job?
items.a: For work statuses, if you do not engage in the permitted activities for over three months, you may lose your status. Consult Immigration if you have no next job yet.

items.q: I lost my residence card. What should I do?
items.a: First file a lost-property report at the nearest police station, then apply for "Reissuance of Residence Card" at Immigration within 14 days.

items.q: I accidentally overstayed. What should I do?
items.a: Go to Immigration immediately and explain your situation. Depending on circumstances, "Special Permission to Stay" may be granted. Leaving it as is may result in illegal overstay.

items.q: Do I need to change status if I get married?
items.a: If you marry a Japanese national or a permanent resident, you may change to "Spouse or Child of Japanese National" or "Spouse or Child of Permanent Resident". Prepare the required documents and apply.

items.q: What happens to a spouse visa after divorce?
items.a: Once the marriage ends, you cannot maintain a spouse status. If you wish to continue living in Japan, consider changing to another status (e.g., work or long-term resident).

items.q: What procedures are required when a child is born?
items.a: Within 30 days after birth, apply for "Permission to Acquire Status of Residence". The child's status will be based on the parents' status.

items.q: How long does screening take?
items.a: It depends on type and timing, but typically about 2 weeks to 1 month. It may take longer during busy seasons.

items.q: What documents are required for a visa application?
items.a: It varies by case, but typically include an application form, photo, passport, residence card, and an employment contract or enrollment certificate, etc.

items.q: How can I obtain permanent residency?
items.a: In principle, you need 10+ years of residence in Japan, stable income and a tax record. See the official Immigration website for details.

items.q: Where can I apply for a visa?
items.a: In Japan, apply at the Immigration Services Bureau with jurisdiction over your address. From overseas, apply at a Japanese embassy or consulate.

items.q: How reliable are AI answers?
items.a: AIVisa's answers are for reference only. Policies and practices may change. Always check the latest official information and consult a professional (e.g., gyoseishoshi) if needed.

items.q: How do I change the address on my residence card?
items.a: Report the change at your municipal office within 14 days. The new address will be printed on the back of the card.

items.q: Can I work part-time on a Temporary Visitor visa?
items.a: No. Paid activities (part-time jobs, work) are not permitted on a Temporary Visitor visa.

items.q: How can students work part-time legally?
items.a: With "Permission to Engage in Activity Other Than That Permitted", students may work up to 28 hours per week. Please follow the rules.

items.q: I plan to leave Japan but wish to return. What should I do?
items.a: Use a re-entry permit (or deemed re-entry permit) to avoid losing your status. Check this before departure.

items.q: My result hasn't come yet. How can I check the status?
items.a: Immigration generally does not provide case status by phone. Please wait for the result or check directly at the submitting counter.

items.q: I'm not confident handling the procedures myself.
items.a: If you are unsure about complex procedures and document preparation, consider hiring a gyoseishoshi (administrative scrivener) with proxy filing authorization.
